subject: Discovery: Data audit & PII guardrails — recap & action items
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Park <alicia.park@leviahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery: Data audit & PII guardrails — recap & action items

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier. Quick recap from our side and a proposed list of next steps so we can align internal stakeholders on scope & constraints. High-level goal we heard: enable short PII-aware retrieval and retrieval-augmented generation for clinician notes while preserving auditability and strict retention controls.

Key pain points you mentioned:
- Clinical notes contain direct identifiers and free-text PHI; current stack (internal search + vector DB) lacks granular redaction and immutable audit logs.
- Security team requires proof of redaction, per-field retention enforcement, and an auditable trail for model inputs/outputs.
- Response latency target is 200ms p50 for simple retrieval + RAG snippets; current config has spikes up to ~800ms.

Current stack (what you said):
- Ingest pipeline: Kafka -> transformer preprocessor -> vector DB (self-hosted)
- Models: mixed use of open LLMs hosted on VMs + custom on-prem embeddings
- Identity/KMS: AWS KMS with customer-managed CMKs

Success criteria (initial PoC):
1) No raw PII leaves Levia environment (redaction-on-ingest or token-level redaction in flight)
2) Retention enforcement window configurable per field (e.g., 90 days for PHI excerpts, 365 days for metadata)
3) Immutable audit logs for every inference request and model output (searchable, exportable)
4) Meet latency target for 95% of requests under realistic traffic

Risks / open questions:
- Which fields you need redacted vs allowed as hashed/pseudonymized values?
- Will audit logs be stored in your VPC or are we permitted to stream logs to a Redwood-managed instance for PoC?
- Do you require HSM-backed keys for inference-level encryption (we support KMS/HSM integrations)?

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll share a short POC SOW and a checklist for PII mapping (attached).
2) Security deep-dive with your infra & security engineers — can we schedule 45 mins next week?
3) Small test harness: ingest 10k anonymized notes (we can mask locally) and validate redaction + audit log generation.

Can you confirm: preferred time slots Tue/Wed next week (10–12 PST) and whether logs must remain in your VPC?

Thanks — I’ll pause the SOW edits until I hear which option you prefer on logs.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: redwood-poc-sow-draft.pdf, pii-handling-checklist.xlsx
From: Alicia Park <alicia.park@leviahealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: security@leviahealth.com
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery: Data audit & PII guardrails — recap & action items

Thanks, Kimberly — this is helpful. A few clarifications:

- Redaction: We need deterministic redaction for patient name, SSN, and MRN. Free-text PHI should be redacted by default; we can allow hashed identifiers for linkage.
- Logs: For the POC, logs must stay in our AWS account (S3 with server-side encryption) — we cannot stream raw model inputs to any third-party. Exported audit artifacts (redacted) can be shared.
- KMS/HSM: We currently use AWS KMS with CMKs; we will evaluate HSM for production but not blocking for the POC.

I can do Tue 13 Apr 2027 10:30–11:15 PDT for the security deep-dive. Will invite our infra lead, Jordan.

Alicia
Director of Product, Levia Health
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Park <alicia.park@leviahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery: Data audit & PII guardrails — recap & action items

Alicia — great, thanks for the clarifications. Confirming next steps and small scope adjustments for the POC based on your answers:

Updated POC scope (short):
- Ingest 10k clinician notes with deterministic redaction applied pre-ingest in your account (we will provide the mapping script and runbook).
- Audit logs: Redwood agent will write redact-only metadata (request id, timestamp, redaction summary, hash of redacted fields) to an S3 bucket in your AWS account under a prefix we agree on. No raw prompts or raw outputs will be exported.
- Encryption: Use your CMKs for server-side encryption of stored artifacts.
- Latency baseline: run 1k synthetic requests to validate p95 under 300ms — we’ll iterate if needed.

Please find attached: updated SOW draft (light edits), and a PII mapping checklist we discussed.

Action items assigned:
- Alicia/Levia: Confirm S3 prefix and create a service-role for Redwood agent to write logs (or confirm you prefer us to connect through an agent deployed in your VPC).
- Kimberly/Redwood: Prepare the mapping script & test harness; propose a PoC schedule and kickoff doc by EOD Wed.
- Karthik: I’ve looped you in to help with the test harness and latency profiling.

Scheduling: I’ll send a calendar invite for Tue 13 Apr 2027 10:30 PDT; if that doesn’t work for Marcus/Karthik we’ll propose alternates.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Kim

Attachments: redwood-poc-sow-draft.pdf, pii-handling-checklist.xlsx
From: security@leviahealth.com <security@leviahealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Park <alicia.park@leviahealth.com>, Jordan Hale <jordan.hale@leviahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery: Data audit & PII guardrails — recap & action items

Kimberly / Redwood team —

Jordan and I confirmed the 10:30am PDT slot for Tue 13 Apr. For the meeting please bring:
- Proposed IAM role policy doc (least privilege write to S3 prefix)
- A one-pager on redaction approach (deterministic + regex fallback)
- Audit log schema (we only need metadata: request id, timestamp, redaction-tags, hash of redacted-fields)

We will not provide production data for the PoC. Please ensure test data follows our anonymization checklist. Looking forward to the kickoff.

— Levia Security Team
